A-DISPATCH: a SMSP's scheduler issues at most 1 warp instruction a SMSP-cycle, of any kind, uniform included (the SM's 4 partitions each with one warp scheduler and one dispatch unit: Volta-onward architecture whitepapers)

A-TENSOR: the tensor cores do at most the data sheet's dense peak a SM-clock for the form's type, a 2:4 sparse form twice that on its logical k; a form's SMSP-cycles are its MACs over a quarter of it. L40S (data sheet at 2520 MHz, 142 SMs): dense MACs a SM-clock s8 and e4m3 1024, s4 2048, f16/bf16 with f32 accumulate 512, tf32 256; no b1 figure (BMMA on DS_issue alone)

A-PIPE: the alu pipe (Nsight Compute: logic, bit manipulation, integer except IMAD/IMUL) at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.9: 32-bit add, compare/min/max, bitwise, shift), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-PIPE: the fmaheavy pipe (Nsight Compute: IMAD/IMUL, integer dot products, HFMA2) at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.9: 32-bit integer multiply-add 64, FP16x2 128 results = 64 HFMA2 lanes), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction; FFMA, on fmaheavy or fmalite, is held by DS_issue

A-PIPE: XU (transcendentals and conversions) at 16 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.9: 32-bit reciprocal, rsqrt, log2, exp2, sin, cos), 8 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-PIPE: FLO/POPC at 16 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.9: count of leading zeros, most significant non-sign bit, population count), 8 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction
A-PIPE: SHFL at 32 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.9: warp shuffle), 4 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-SMEM: shared memory serves a request's distinct banks together, at most 128 B a SM-clock (Programming Guide 'Shared Memory': 32 banks, each 32 bits a clock), reads and writes alike; a broadcast load or a store to one address moves as little as one word, so each LDS/LDSM/STS warp instruction holds one request, 4 SMSP-cycles, whatever its width
